title: Senjak Market, 3rd prize
thumbnailDescription: Architectural Studio Saurus won the THIRD ENHANCED PRIZE for the competition design of the Senjak market building with an underground garage and public areas in 2010. The president of the competition jury was Vasilije Milunović, a full professor at the Faculty of Architecture.
client: Municipality of Savski venac and DAB
descriptionLong:
Architectural studio Saurus won the third enhanced prize at the Senjak market competition. The second prize was not awarded. THE CITY MUNICIPALITY OF SAVSKI VENAC, Belgrade in cooperation with the ASSOCIATION OF ARCHITECTS OF BELGRADE announced a general public anonymous survey urban-architectural competition for the design of the "Senjak" market. The jury will evaluate the competition entries according to the following framework criteria:
- Compliance with the conditions of the brief and the competition program;
- The design concept appropriate to the importance of the location;
- The functionality of the market design;
- Contemporary tendencies in the design of city spaces and a modern traffic solution;
- The relationship of the proposed design to the surroundings.
- Rationality and economy of the offered solution. Competition Jury:
Prof. Vasilije Milunović, B.Sc. Arch., President and members:
Ljubica Popović, B.Sc. Econ., M.Sc. Žaklina Gligorijević, B.Sc. Arch., Dragan Ćorović, B.Sc. Elec. Eng., Nina Mitranić, B.Sc. Arch., Slobodan Ristić, B.Sc. Arch., Aleksandar Nedeljković, B.Sc. Arch. The complexity of the problem was inspiring in sculpting the hard-to-reach unity of many influences, producing a rich, multi-layered, and well-founded conceptual design with a lot of potential for further development.

title: Square in Beočin, Novi Sad, 1st prize
thumbnailDescription: Architectural Studio Saurus won the FIRST PRIZE for the competition design of the square in Beočin. The jury members were the president of the jury Bogdan Cvejić, 'Lafarge' architect from Paris Leopold Lombard, and professor at the Faculty of Architecture in Belgrade Zoran Lazović.
descriptionLong:
Architectural studio Saurus won the competition. Excerpt from the Beočin municipality website www.beocin.rs:
The company Lafarge BFC d.o.o. announced a competition for the conceptual design of a square in Beočin, which will be built in cooperation with the municipality of Beočin. Based on the announced competition, a total of 48 entries were received. The international jury unanimously decided that the first prize for the conceptual design for the construction of the square in Beočin should go to the documentation under the code "Lepeza" (Fan). It is a joint work created by the married couple Tomić, Jelena and Srđan from Aranđelovac.
Guided by the criteria that the idea should primarily be feasible, then that the square should be functional, i.e., serve the purpose of gathering citizens, and that it should fit well into the existing environment, the jury unanimously decided that the winning work should be the authorial work of the young married couple from Aranđelovac.
The jury members were the president of the jury Bogdan Cvejić, "Lafarge's" architect from Paris Leopold Lombard, professor of the Faculty of Architecture in Belgrade Zoran Lazović, professor of the Faculty of Architecture in Novi Sad Milica Kostreš and president of the Association of Architects of Novi Sad N.K.
Based on the selected conceptual design, the project for the building permit, consulting, design supervision over the execution of the square.

title: Japanese fountain 3rd prize
thumbnailDescription: Architectural Studio Saurus won the THIRD PRIZE for the competition design on the theme of a Japanese fountain in Kalemegdan, organized by GSP Belgrade in 2010. The president of the competition jury was Branislav Mitrović, a full professor at the Faculty of Architecture.
descriptionLong:
Architectural studio Saurus won the third prize in the competition. The idea was too demanding for the investor considering the deadlines for realization. We dedicate this fountain on Kalemegdan to the Japanese people as a sign of gratitude for the help they provided us in difficult times. Japan is a country both spiritually and spatially distant. In a time when physical distances are erased via the "world wide web", we tried to get closer in this global virtual world and give our gift to every Japanese person. They will see it on Google Maps, Google Earth, internet applications that allow easy viewing of the entire surface of the planet in the form of satellite images via the internet. At the confluence of two rivers, in an old fortress full of historical layers, they will see it as one of the basic characters from the Japanese script that denotes the essential ingredient of nature - water. If for any reason they wander from afar among these walls, they will be surprised to hear how people in Belgrade clumsily but unusually often repeat, in fact, every time they drink water, a sound familiar to them, the sonic part of the same concept - Mizu! Nowhere on the fountain, in the mass media, are instructions for use highlighted. Citizens gradually conquer the urban secret that is transmitted orally, like city gossip. We predict that this immaterial aspect of discovery in the collective consciousness of the city, constantly renewing itself through new generations, will last longer than the material itself, which is another bow to Japanese philosophy. On the location, we corrected an error in space by which the space defined by four trees is treated as an independent whole. The potential of this isolated island was unlocked and released to spill over the entire plateau at the level. In the ground floor treatment, this is reflected in one height quota and a sea of granite cubes on which concentric circles of greenery float. Thus, we activated the entire square in the function of the fountain with peripherally arranged seating positions for rest and observation. Competition Jury:
Branislav Mitrović, B.Sc. Arch., full professor at the Faculty of Architecture and members: Darijan Mihajlović, member of the city council, Tetsuya Tsubota, first secretary of the Embassy of Japan in Serbia, Marina Andrić, art historian and Ksenija Kostić, B.Sc. Arch. GSP Belgrade.

descriptionLong:
A house project in the zone of individual construction on the edge of the green zone. It is positioned on the northern side of the plot, oriented towards the southern intimate courtyard.
The building has a basement+GF+1+Attic. The slight height difference of the plot of 1.50m was used to form a semi-buried basement on the northern side which serves as a garage, boiler room, and firewood storage, with a warm connection - a staircase to the ground floor.
The ground floor of the building is at the elevation of the upper southern courtyard and is intended for a living room, while the night zone is on the 1st floor. The attic is a storage room.
The shaping of the building is calm, modern, and subordinated to its residential function. The form of the building consists of two basic cubes whose proportions and intersection create a stable composition.

title: Almeks Hotel Tamiš Pančevo
thumbnailDescription: Architectural Studio Saurus. A city block in the immediate vicinity of the Tamiš River, the bridge, and the quay, right at the 'entrance' to Pančevo. The reconstruction of the hotel and the addition of a floor are proposed, as well as the addition of various facilities on the plot through six phases of construction.
descriptionLong:
Context
The intervention area is located in the immediate vicinity of the Tamiš river, the bridge, and the quay, right at the "entrance" via the old road (main road BG - Vršac (Romania)) and in the immediate vicinity of the city center. The physical structure of the surrounding urban fabric is traditional block construction of predominantly individual ground floor+1 buildings. Description of the Architectural solution with implementation dynamics
Architectural Studio Saurus. A city block in the immediate vicinity of the Tamiš river, the bridge, and the quay, right at the "entrance" to Pančevo. The reconstruction of the hotel and the addition of a floor are proposed, as well as the addition of various facilities on the plot through six phases of construction. Energy efficiency is improved through the energy rehabilitation of the hotel facade and its reconstruction.
The designed space can be divided into four sub-units by purpose - a hotel, a shopping center with a garage, a business unit, a residential-business unit, and a public space.
The total realized developed gross area is 27508 m2.
The total realized developed net area is 24385 m2.
Occupancy index (Iz) 50% (compared to the existing Iz 14%) Integration
The problem in the urban fabric was created by the construction of an oversized freestanding object in a traditional block matrix of fragmented structure. The inversion of built-unbuilt is in complete contrast to the context.
The principle of integration was applied as a universal method for solving complex problems. The integration of Hotel Tamiš takes place on several levels:
- at the level of the built physical structure within the block (part of the belonging block) as well as the block itself (part of the belonging block) into the surrounding urban fabric - by peripheral construction.
- at the level of content - by integrating the hotel's content on the ground floor with the contents of the belonging block that will be built, as well as by introducing new contents that are attractive to a large number of visitors.
- by activating pedestrian flows, i.e., retaining existing pedestrian flows and forming new pedestrian flows, i.e., enabling a direct connection of the center with the river and other planned urban points by including it in the international tourist offer (accommodation of the city of Belgrade (practically at the same distance from the City Assembly of Belgrade as the hotel chains in New Belgrade) i.e., the main road Belgrade-Romania). Activation of the block's interior
Hotel Tamiš, with its free-standing brutally shaped corpus, occupies the central part of the block, leaving the regulation line free.
Physical structure - the structure of Hotel Tamiš, similar to a flower - develops in the existing grid over the entire surface of the plot's ground floor, forming solid-void (green) spaces. Peripheral construction could not be simply applied because it produces the problem of conflict between backyards and the hotel, i.e., a hotel inside the block. The solution was found in integration at the ground floor/parterre level - where it is common for the entire complex in its purpose and structure. The roofs of the ground floor wings of the hotel (restaurant) become green platforms - a new inner courtyard. Various pedestrian flows are allowed through the spaces of the complex, motivated by a carefully planned layout of different purposes and existing attractors (Tamiš, bus stops, Army House). Energy efficiency and ecology
The applied materials and equipment need to meet the highest standards in this area - energy efficiency and savings, green energy production, and the use of technologically advanced solutions. Energy efficiency was achieved through the energy rehabilitation of the hotel's facade and its reconstruction. The planned objects fully respect these principles - by their shape, spatial organization, careful orientation, and technical solutions for heating (heat pumps and solar panels for heating hot water), lighting (LED lighting, high-class equipment), and rainwater reuse. Roof gardens are planned to reduce CO2 emissions and achieve a better microclimate of the block.

title: House in Sremska Mitrovica
thumbnailDescription: Architectural Studio Saurus. Conceptual design, building permit project, interior design, consulting, and design supervision for a family house in Sremska Mitrovica.
descriptionLong:
The family building of GF (Ground Floor) floors, auxiliary buildings of GF and Basement+GF, and an outdoor pool are positioned on the regulation line towards the street and within the building lines.
A warm and comfortable home atmosphere is achieved with a traditional language and construction techniques in combination with modern technologies. The interior design is conceived in such a way that the inner and outer spaces together form an intimate whole separated from the public space.
The main building is set along the northern edge of the plot, oriented mostly to the south, leaving room for a courtyard in the southern part, while the auxiliary building perpendicular to it separates the garden in the western part of the plot set back from the street.
The ground floor design envisages dividing the plot into two levels to fit into the street profile which is at a slight slope. The building itself with its appurtenant plateau and pool finished with wooden decking is raised in relation to the rest of the yard.

title: Mirra Capital Belgrade Madridska 8
thumbnailDescription: Architectural Studio Saurus. Conceptual design, building permit project, interior design, consulting, and design supervision for a residential-commercial building with a gross area of 3470m2.
descriptionLong:
Architectural Studio Saurus created the conceptual design, building permit project, interior design, consulting, and design supervision for a residential and commercial building on the corner of Bulevar kralja Aleksandra and Madridska Street with a gross area of 3470m2 with 40 apartments. The location has high potential in the planned further development of the city based on the Master Plan of Belgrade 2021. It is located at the entrance to the central zone of Belgrade, in the zone of the newly planned sub-center and in the middle of the stretch between the newly planned representative space Promenade Pašina česma on the site of the old tram turnaround across the park-square and the newly planned business center at the intersection of Bulevar kralja Aleksandra and Ustanička.
The building is positioned along the building lines towards Bulevar kralja Aleksandra (the building line coincides with the regulation line) and Madridska Street (the building line is 3m away from the regulation line), closing the block on the corner in an L shape and leaning with its gable walls at the height of the planned maximum heights of the neighbors, which differs significantly. The complexity of the height regulation problem is a consequence of the large elevation difference between the two streets and their different importance and profile. Viewed from Bulevar kralja Aleksandra, the ground floor with commercial space is a separate entity - the base of the building, the framed 6 floors of the building with residential function are the body, and the set-back floor with a canopy forms the cornice of the building. Secondary plasticity is defined by a strict grid of horizontals and verticals that frame the windows and loggias, and a rhythmic intertwining of two types of materialization. However, the building is formally separated into two units horizontally, each fitting into the planned street profile. The lower part of the building with three residential floors is treated as an interpolation that starts the future row of buildings along Madridska Street. The connecting element is the protruding "storefront" of the commercial space that bends from the Boulevard and underlines the interpolation, framing and unifying the two facades. The part of the building below the 0.00 elevation, i.e., the commercial floor that underlines the entire building, from Madridska Street is treated as a "service", vehicular entrance, and garage on two levels, within which is inserted, until the realization of the Detailed Regulation Plan, the only possible pedestrian entrance to the building.

title: Mirra Capital Belgrade Bulevar 414
thumbnailDescription: A rhythmic, moderate facade combining warm brick, white surfaces, and dark metal parts attempts to connect the dignity of one of Belgrade's main streets with the warmth and intimacy of a home.
descriptionLong:
The location at the intersection of Bulevar kralja Aleksandra and Mite Ružića, i.e., Katarine Milovuk, closes the corner of a compact high-density block defined by the Detailed Regulation Plan.
Functionally, the maximum was extracted from the given conditions with the achieved commercial space on the ground floor. The residential-commercial building contains 50 high-quality apartments of optimal surface area and diverse structure, and the necessary number of parking spaces on three garage levels.
Given that it is among the first to start the realization of the plan for the further expansion of Bulevar kralja Aleksandra from Cvetko's market onwards, the building has no support in the existing context, but rather defines it itself. A rhythmic, moderate facade in a combination of warm brick, white surfaces, and dark metal parts with a specially articulated, but not exaggerated corner, attempts to connect the dignity and public character of one of Belgrade's main streets with the warmth and intimacy of a home. Building on previous brick examples, but in a fresh way, using the possibility of choosing modern brick products for a more subtle combination of contrasting materials, with the quality of energy efficiency that far exceeds former standards.

title: Family house on a hill in Belgrade
thumbnailDescription: Little Fortress. The house optimally blends with the terrain on several cascading levels along which the interior spaces open up to the sun and the view like a spiral flower and extend onto open terraces.
descriptionLong: A family house for a family of four on a demanding steep terrain is positioned halfway up the slope to open a view over the neighbors. The house optimally blends with the terrain on several cascading levels along which the inner spaces open up to the sun and the view like a spiral flower and extend to open terraces. The entire complex with a pool is bounded by retaining stone walls and fences, forming a compact whole reminiscent of a small family fortress. "Well, they'll have a harder time tearing down this little fortress..."

title: Šumadinka house in Banja Aranđelovac
thumbnailDescription: Šumadinka, a house in Banja Aranđelovac, is a timeless response to the traditional context of good hosts and the green, hilly Šumadija idyll. The house is optimally positioned on a gently sloping terrain.
descriptionLong: Šumadinka, a house in Banja Aranđelovac, is a timeless response to the traditional context of good hosts and the green, hilly Šumadija idyll. The house is optimally positioned on a gently sloping terrain. The main problem at the location was the conflict between the need to open living rooms to the view down the hill, and the need to open to the sun up the hill. The project enabled both by dividing the house into a sleeping and a living wing, which is freely oriented on three sides. Natural materials were used - clay, wood, and stone. Energy efficiency and indoor comfort were achieved by using modernized traditional brick blocks with high thermal insulation properties that allow the house to "breathe" with minimal costs of maintaining thermal comfort.

title: Competition Savski square Belgrade
thumbnailDescription: It is precisely from the love between a father and son that Serbia began to grow like an oak, initially as the Nemanjić family tree, to further continue with branches reaching through the centuries. Savski square is organized as an Oak growing from the center.
descriptionLong:
By the scheduled deadline, a total of 25 competition entries were submitted.
The jury worked in the following composition:
President of the Jury: Prof. Janez Koželj, architect, representative of the Association of Architects of Serbia
Vice President of the Jury: Milutin Folić, architect, Chief Urbanist of the City of Belgrade and members:
Osama Al Hassan, landscape architect, representative of the Client
Jovan Mitrović, architect, representative of the Association of Architects of Serbia
Dr. Milena Kordić, architect, representative of the Association of Architects of Serbia
The jury made the following decisions:
• First prize "Fenwick Iribarren Architects", Madrid, Spain
• Second prize "Medprostor" d.o.o., Ljubljana, Slovenia
• Third prize: "SWA Group (SWA)", California, USA, associates: "CEP" - Center for Urban Development Planning, Belgrade
• Purchase 1: "Arhitektura ARSA", Novi Pazar, Republic of Serbia (Damir Rastoder, Admir Bibić, Emrah Bronja, Armin Redžepagić)
• Purchase 2: InSite, a division of KEO International Consultants", Abu Dhabi, UAE
• Purchase 3, 4 and 5 were not awarded. Savski square - Hrastko
Stefan Nemanja is in the focus of the square, in front of the entrance to the National Museum of the History of Serbia, as a guardian of the gate, a portal to the future. Nemanja was a ruler, a man of the sword, a name derived from "neman" (monster). He named one of his sons Rastko, after growth, or oak (hrast), the sacred Serbian tree. Rastko became St. Sava, the spiritual leader of the Serbian people. It is precisely from the love between a father and son that Serbia began to grow like an oak, initially as the Nemanjić family tree, to further continue with branches reaching through the centuries. Savski square is organized as an Oak that grows from the center, forming organic fractal cells in its crown. Each cell is one open room, an island for different activities, which change from time to time. They can be related to the Museum of the History of Serbia, like the mentioned theme of the Nemanjić family tree, or some other branch chosen from the rich and long Serbian history, or something completely different from the domain of popular art, shopping, entertainment...

title: House settlement in Malawi, Africa
thumbnailDescription: A house settlement in the capital of Malawi in Central Africa. The small neighborhood community consists of nine standard market-oriented houses and one owner's villa. Fenced and controlled access, shared maintenance, and installations.
descriptionLong: The location is very favorable, on an elevation above the city with a beautiful view of the surrounding mountain landscape, and good traffic connections. A special problem is fitting into the triangular shape of the plot and the sloping terrain, with the required high population density and the separation of the owner's villa as a distinct, physically and visually isolated entity. The cultural context of this settlement is not Africa itself, but the global market. A temperature that ranges from +15 to +35 does not require a special thermal envelope, which allows for freer facade design.

thumbnailDescription: A villa with a pool in the capital of Malawi in Central Africa. The slope of the terrain is used to separate the villa from the other houses in the settlement, thereby allowing southern orientation of the living zone with large glass surfaces overlooking the surrounding mountains.
descriptionLong: The location is very favorable, on an elevation above the city with a beautiful view of the surrounding mountain landscape, and good traffic connections. descriptionLong: Packom commercial complex Belgrade. Landscaping. Facade. Interior. These are a series of ad-hoc solutions ranging from conceptual to main projects in the domain of plot landscaping, architectural treatment of the building that builds upon the existing structure, and the interior of the commercial space with very short deadlines for realization. A combination of brick and dark aluminum joinery with large glass surfaces was used on the facade, a rhythm also applied to the ground floor with tactile clinker paving with islands of greenery that do not interfere with the functionality of the production process while simultaneously defining regular observable open spaces, with a specially emphasized square in front of the building entrance.

descriptionLong: Packom commercial complex Belgrade. Landscaping. Facade. Interior. Open space commercial area with glass partitions for physical and acoustic, but not visual isolation. A contrast of tactile rustic brick, untreated raw concrete structure, warm wood, and smooth marble with gold and dark metal accents. descriptionLong: Main project for the adaptation of an existing building in the gray phase into a hotel with 76 beds in 32 rooms and a restaurant. With very limited funds, along with predefined proportions and arrangements of openings and the roof, a harmonious whole was formed by dividing the facades into a base in stone, a body in light plaster, and a floor - cornice by using shallow plasticity and fine shades in the final finish. A hotel equipped with a modern installation system is planned, which is synchronized by the project both mutually and with the inherited concrete structure.
